stem: During electron transport in mitochondria, what happens to protons that enables chemiosmotic ATP synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: They freely equilibrate across an unsealed outer membrane only
options.misconception: Outer membrane is porous; the relevant barrier is the inner membrane.
options.explanation: Complexes pump across the inner membrane.

options.label: B
options.text: They diffuse into the nucleus to activate transcription

options.label: C
options.text: They are consumed as the carbon skeleton of glucose
options.misconception: Protons are not incorporated into CO2 carbon.
options.explanation: CO2 carbons come from substrate carbons.

options.label: D
options.text: They are pumped from the matrix to the intermembrane space
options.misconception: None; proton pumping creates the intermembrane gradient.
options.explanation: OpenStax: protons are pumped from the mitochondrial matrix to the intermembrane space.

options.label: E
options.text: They are stored inside ATP before hydrolysis
options.misconception: ATP stores phosphoryl transfer energy, not a proton pool.
options.explanation: The proton gradient is across the membrane.

context: Learning objective: ETC pumps protons out of the matrix.
imageCaption: Cellular respiration: glycolysis -> pyruvate -> acetyl-CoA -> citric cycle carriers -> ETC/ATP synthase; O2 terminal acceptor; fermentation regenerates NAD+.
